compiled_state.description:
## Context / Problem
CloudWatch alarm `rebar-bridge-run-failures` entered ALARM at 2026-11-03 11:41 PST. Scheduled `reconcile-bridge` runs 41693706227 (10:25 PST), 41703055677 (11:25 PST) and 41712353911 (12:24 PST) all failed identically; the 09:24 PST run and earlier passed. Each failing run dies in `src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py` `_read_blob_bytes`: `git cat-file blob 36823c918daf:lock.json` exceeds `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS` (5.0 s), raises `RefLockTimeoutError`, and the pass lock fails CLOSED (`ReconcileLockError: cannot determine pass-lock state`), so no reconcile pass runs. The lock itself is released (released=True, fence 5, written 09:42:30 PST).

## Root cause (one experiment so far)
The bridge workflow checks out with `filter: blob:none`, and every ref-lock fetch of `refs/reconciler/*` (the workflow's "Sync reconciler lock refs" step and `_fetch_ref`) inherits that partial-clone filter, so the payload blob is NOT local. `cat-file blob` therefore performs a lazy promisor fetch over the network, but ADR 0121 §10 (consolidating ADR 0031) budgets it as a LOCAL op (5 s; remote push/fetch get 30 s). In a fresh blobless clone on the operator host the first read of that exact blob took 4.44 s and the cached repeat 0.02 s, so a slower runner crosses 5 s. Unchecked: why it began at 10:25 PST and not earlier.

## Approach
Classify object reads by what they may do, not where the object usually lives: in a partial clone ANY object read can lazily fetch. So every object read in `_ref_lock.py` takes `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS`: both `cat-file blob` calls in `_read_blob_bytes`, and `_object_type` (`cat-file -t <oid>`) for ALL its callers — the read path, and the write path `_cas_advance` reached from `acquire`, `release`, heartbeat, `set_gate` and `set_pause`. `set_gate`/`set_pause` can reach `_cas_advance` without any prior read, so a legacy blob tip there is also a lazy fetch; one rule for every object read avoids per-caller reasoning. In a full clone or for a present object these return in milliseconds, so the larger bound only matters when a fetch actually happens. Ref-only ops (`update-ref`, `rev-parse`, `mktree`) are not object reads of fetched content and keep `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`. This is portable (no CI-specific step; any partial clone benefits) and adds no mechanism. Fail-closed semantics are unchanged: a 30 s timeout still raises `RefLockTimeoutError` and is treated as HELD. ADR 0121 §10 ("Fail-closed reads and bounded timeouts", the authoritative consolidated record) is amended to say payload blob reads take the remote budget because a partial clone may fetch them lazily. The archived ADR 0031 is kept verbatim as the evidence record and is not edited.

## Files
- `src/rebar/reconciler/_ref_lock.py` — `_read_blob_bytes` timeouts.
- `docs/adr/0121-reconciler-architecture-consolidated-record.md` — §10 timeout sentence amendment.
- `tests/unit/reconciler/state/test_ref_lock_blob_read_budget.py` — new test.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Both `cat-file blob` reads in `_read_blob_bytes` receive `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS`; a new unit test recording the timeout each `_git` call receives fails before the change and passes after.
- [ ] `_object_type` receives `_REMOTE_TIMEOUT_SECS` from every caller, asserted by the same test on the read path and during a `set_gate` CAS advance over a legacy blob tip.
- [ ] `update-ref` calls in `_ref_lock.py` still receive `_LOCAL_TIMEOUT_SECS`, asserted by the same test.
- [ ] A new test builds a real `--filter=blob:none` clone of a local bare repo holding a `refs/reconciler/lock` commit and shows `read()` returns the released lock state, with the payload blob absent locally before the read.
- [ ] `docs/adr/0121-reconciler-architecture-consolidated-record.md` §10 states that object reads (`cat-file`) use the 30 s remote budget because a partial clone may fetch them lazily; `git diff origin/main -- docs/adr/0031-reconciler-ref-lock.md` is empty.
- [ ] `make lint` exits 0.
- [ ] `make typecheck` exits 0.
- [ ] `pytest tests/unit/reconciler/` exits 0.
- [ ] [non-codebase] The first scheduled `reconcile-bridge` run after the merge succeeds and publishes `bridge_run_failures=0`.
  provenance: production-equivalent / live-call
- [ ] [non-codebase] `rebar-bridge-run-failures` returns to OK.
